_what: Big Steep Fermentables, level B1 of Arlesglad Caverns: a brewery and cellar for wine, beer and kombucha. Ryan's brief, 2026-09-26: try our house styles. Every house style is an entry here, and tools/make-big-steep.py writes the cellar's racks out of this file.
_strength_first: EVERY POUR SAYS HOW STRONG IT IS BEFORE YOU TAKE IT. The street's runtime rule for a drink: a press-to-play control says how long it runs before the press, and a pour says how much alcohol is in it before the pour, because that number is what lets somebody decide. The tool refuses a pour without its strength.
_alcohol_free_first: EVERY HOUSE STYLE COMES WITHOUT ALCOHOL, AND THAT POUR COMES FIRST AND THE SAME SIZE. Many of us do not drink -- medication, recovery, disability, faith, or simply not wanting to -- and a cellar that listed the alcohol-free pour second, smaller, or as a 'mocktail' would be telling those people they are the afterthought. Dead Tired Society's rule about passing: the choice not to is first and the same size. The tool refuses a style whose first pour has alcohol in it, and the vocabulary that makes an alcohol-free drink sound like an imitation.
_kombucha: KOMBUCHA IS NEVER QUITE ZERO, AND SAYS SO. It is fermented, so there is always a trace of alcohol in it, and the trace varies from batch to batch. So its fermented pour gives a ceiling rather than a number, and its alcohol-free pour is the same tea and fruit, not fermented, which is the only honest way to have none. The tool refuses a kombucha that claims a fixed strength.
_no_pressure: NOTHING HERE PRESSES ANYBODY TO DRINK, AND NOTHING COUNTS HOW MUCH. No rounds, no 'one more', no drinking games, nothing glamorising being drunk, and no count of pours. And nothing is good for you: no probiotic, no gut, no antioxidants, no hangover cure. The tool sweeps this file and the published room for all of it, with the checkpoint's negation window so the room can say what it will not do.
_in_the_glass: Each style's `glow` is the colour its light comes through the glass as, in love.css: amber, straw, garnet, stout, haze or hibiscus. It paints the vessel drawn above the style and nothing else; the words say what the drink is.
_ambience: SOMEBODY ELSE'S CELLARS, TO LEAVE ON. Ryan's brief, 2026-09-27: wine cellar ambience videos, 'not an exact fit for the Big Steep, but they'll do'. They are not an exact fit and the room says so: each is somebody else's cellar, bar or tavern with barrels, wood and fire in it, which this cellar has none of, so they are shown as other places to have on rather than as views of this one. Ryan added seven more on 2026-10-19 and asked for the room's videos to take the street's rack and shared screen (rack.js): every video plays where it hangs or goes up on the screen in the rock, which has nothing of its own on it and ships hidden, the Doom Scoop's and Brew and Stew's screen, because the room has no whole list to put on. Being the room's first screen, it is also where the CB puts a video. The order is Ryan's: the first three as they were, then the seven in the order he gave them. Every id was read on the date in ambience_read with yt-dlp: public, not age-gated, not live, on its uploader's own channel, the date it went up, and runtime MEASURED, because the speakeasy's own title says 4 hours and its description says 5 and it runs 4:46:57. ONE OF THEM IS A DOOR: the wine bar's channel has switched off showing it on other sites (playable_in_embed false on 2026-10-19), so it is a link out to YouTube shaped like a door, with no screen button, and check-jukebox.py expects it to refuse the frame. Their titles are quoted as written and the room's sweeps skip them. Their descriptions sell them for sleep, study and focus, and none of that is copied here. THREE OF THE LINKS RYAN GAVE CARRIED A YOUTUBE RADIO LIST (list=RD...), a mix YouTube generates on the fly rather than a playlist anybody keeps. The first was dropped and put back the same evening, 2026-09-27, Ryan's call: 'I don't mind an on-the-fly list', and the two that came with one on 2026-10-19 keep theirs on that call. So those presses open the video and then play on into whatever YouTube's mix picks, and their labels say so: the first video's runtime, and then no runtime, because nobody knows what the mix holds until it plays. Nobody here has checked what comes after the first video; the labels say that too. Nothing musical is hosted here: the music is on its uploaders' channels, behind a press.
